subject: falling space station
title: What If a 77-Ton Space Station Fell on Your Town? In 1979 One Did

scenes.text: What if a 77-ton space station fell out of the sky? In 1979, NASA couldn't say where.
Skylab, America's first space station, was dropping faster than planned. NASA put the odds of debris hitting someone at 1 in 152.
People painted targets on roofs, bought plastic Skylab helmets, and bet on where it would land. A newspaper offered 10,000 dollars for the first piece.
On July 11, 1979, it broke up over the Indian Ocean. The surviving pieces came down across Western Australia, in a strip 150 kilometres wide.
Nobody was hurt. The Shire of Esperance fined NASA 400 dollars for littering. NASA never paid.
Thirty years later, a California radio host and his listeners paid it for them. It's still the biggest thing ever to fall out of orbit uncontrolled.

description:
What if a space station fell out of orbit with no way to steer it? In July 1979 NASA's 77-ton Skylab did exactly that.
NASA estimated a 1 in 152 chance of debris hitting a person; Americans sold Skylab helmets and held crash parties while a San Francisco paper offered 10,000 dollars for the first piece. On 11 July 1979 the station broke up over the Indian Ocean and scattered debris across a strip of Western Australia about 150 kilometres wide. No one was hurt; the Shire of Esperance issued NASA a 400 dollar littering fine that a California radio station finally paid in 2009.
